findings.claim: read_json still tells the user to run `kmctl plugin install again`, a command this change deletes. patch reaches it through drop_old_hook and drop_old_mcp, so a settings.json or .mcp.json that does not parse makes `kmctl plugin patch` refuse with a fix that answers 'No such command'. Reproduced in a scratch repo: `refused: .../.claude/settings.json is not valid JSON (...); fix it, then run kmctl plugin install again`.

Tests for code that is still live went with the old verbs. remove_old_plugin keeps only its happy path (lost: plugin of another repository left alone, user scope, marketplace already gone, uninstall failure stops, claude missing skips). drop_old_hook lost its shared-group and nothing-recorded tests. drop_old_mcp lost 'user scope keeps a current okf-bundle'. uninstall_name, which the refusal message now depends on, lost its parametrized forms (scp URL, port, string). The invalid-settings refusal test went too; it would have caught f1. Port these to call patch, or the functions directly.

This change left orphans and stale comments. _apm_run has no caller now that patch never runs APM. The comment on HARNESSES says '--harness accepts', and the one on DEFAULT_SOURCE says 'unless --source names another'. Neither option exists any more.

Text that is now false: .claude/rules/cli-version-floor.md keeps the heading 'The CLI installs its package' and the constraint name 'the-package-is-installed-by-the-cli', but its body (rightly) says the user installs with apm install. The module docstrings of tests/test_apm_package.py (line 7, 'runs kmctl plugin install --harness claude --source') and tests/test_antigravity.py (line 1, 'kmctl plugin install --harness antigravity') describe a command that is gone.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
`kmctl plugin patch` reads the lock, refuses old entry forms before it refuses a missing package, patches only the harnesses the lock lists, never runs uvx, and the old verbs are gone.
A fresh stamp is green on every gate and every row.
I found no defect that needs a second look, but there are four plain fixes.
One stale refusal message (f1) names the deleted `kmctl plugin install`.
Tests for functions that are still live were deleted along with the verbs (f2).
There is leftover dead code and stale comments (f3), and a rule heading and two test docstrings now say false things (f4).
Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree myself, with a fresh, empty scratch HOME.
Result: `pass` for lint, format, tests and integration, and for eval rows r1 to r7.
`stamp green: e73c649e1f35ca614d202f67dbe5034ad70d4f48d259f871e3e81c09a8cdedd9`.
The state commit was deferred only because the scratch HOME has no git identity.
Code read in full: plugin.py, the plugin_patch command in __init__.py, and the doctor.py, antigravity.py, briefing.py and scaffold.py diffs.
patch checks for an old entry form before it checks the lock, as the plan orders.
Harnesses come from the lock's deployed_files.
The claude cleanup runs only when the lock lists claude, and antigravity only at project scope.
`--undo` deletes only `.agents/plugins/kmctl/`.
The Next line, `--json`, and the exit code 1 on refusal match the plan.
Every doctor fix now names apm install, the apm.yml ref or kmctl plugin patch.
The antigravity rpartition still splits APM_FIX correctly, because APM_FIX contains no '; '.
Eval rows: I read every test the rows run.

r1: tests assert on the written folder against plugin_files, the Stop handler being gone, no uvx calls, hook and stale okf-bundle removal at both scopes with the 'apm install again' note, the old-plugin calls, byte-identical files on a second run, and the JSON keys and Next line.
r2: tests assert exit 1, the named apm install, the string-form and v0.3.0-layout uninstall names (with -g at user scope), and the new entry.
r3: tests assert that only the folder changed, and exit 0 when there is nothing to undo.
r4: tests assert exit 2 and 'No such command' for each old verb, that `plugin` lists only `patch`, a regex over every doctor fix across the BREAKS table, and init's Next line.
r5: tests assert the README's three harness sections and each step, the commands.md headings, and the ADR 0021/0019 links.
r6: runs real APM 0.33.0 from a served tree, then patch, init, doctor (exit 0), undo and uninstall, and checks that nothing is left.
All of these assert their fails_when.
APM behaviour behind the docs: I checked `uvx --offline --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm --help`, `update --help`, `uninstall --help` and `install --help`.
`apm update` and `apm uninstall -g` exist, and `install` takes `--target` with commas.
The okf-bundle re-install claim matches spike plugin-patch/1.

Docs: I read the README install section, the commands.md patch section, both how-tos, ADR 0021, the ADR 0019/0014 corrections, the index, the log, the manifesto, the architecture overview, the tutorial and the explanations.
They match the code: the refusal order, the user-scope note, `--undo` output, the anchors (#7-to-remove-kmctl, #before-you-start) and the Next line.
I reproduced f1 with the worktree's kmctl in a scratch repo.
f1: `read_json`'s 'not valid JSON' message still says 'run kmctl plugin install again'.
patch surfaces it as the fix in its refusal.
Change it to a fix that exists, as the 'not a JSON object' branch already does ('run the command again').
f2: Coverage for remove_old_plugin, drop_old_hook, drop_old_mcp and uninstall_name went with test_plugin.py and test_plugin_remove.py.
These functions are still live, and patch's refusal relies on uninstall_name.
Restore those cases against patch or the functions directly, and add a test for the invalid-JSON refusal.
f3: Remove `_apm_run`, and fix the HARNESSES and DEFAULT_SOURCE comments that name the removed --harness and --source options.
f4: Retitle the rule and rename its constraint to match its body.
Update the two test module docstrings.
Possibly pre-existing, and not shown here: a later okf pin bump could leave a stale okf-bundle in `.agents/mcp_config.json` that APM skips.
patch removes a stale okf-bundle only for claude, so doctor's antigravity.okf-mcp fix (apm install, then patch) would not clear it.
Worth a spike when OKF_COMMIT next moves.
`kmctl plugin patch --undo --scope user --json` reports `scope: project`.
That is harmless, since undo only touches the repository, but slightly odd.
When the old-layout lock has a git entry from a fork, `_old_entry` falls back to naming `JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm` for uninstall.
This is an edge case that carried over from the old install code.
